name: Viking 1 Orbiter
manufacturer: NASA Langley Research Center / Martin Marietta
best_known_for: Companion orbiter to Viking-1 lander — relay + 50000 surface images at 150-300 m/pixel, the first global Mars map. Operated 1976-1980
credit: The orbital half of NASA's Viking 1 mission — the first US Mars orbiter and one of two near-identical Viking orbiters that returned ~50,000 surface images at 150-300 m/pixel between 1976 and 1980. Launched 1975-08-20 from Cape Canaveral on a Titan IIIE-Centaur, Viking 1 entered Mars orbit 1976-06-19; the orbiter spent a month surveying candidate landing sites before releasing the Viking 1 lander 1976-07-20 to the first successful US Mars landing at Chryse Planitia. The orbiter then continued as a science platform for nearly four more years, building the first global topographic + thermal map of Mars, surveying Phobos + Deimos, and acting as a UHF relay for the lander. Out of attitude-control gas 1980-08-07. Deliberately raised to a 357 × 33614 km park orbit that's expected to remain stable through ~2024 (decayed ~2025 per Aerospace Corp re-entry forecast).
